prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that Russell M. Nelson dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Russell M. Nelson dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church from 2018 to 2025, dedicated the Rome Italy Temple in 2019, the first temple in Italy. He also dedicated Sapporo Japan (2016) and Concepción Chile (2018) and rededicated Sydney Australia (1991) and Nuku'alofa Tonga (2007). Later he rededicated Washington D.C. (2022) and Manti Utah (2024).

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Manti Utah (rededicated 2024); Washington D.C. (rededicated 2022); Deseret Peak Utah (2024); and others.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Rome Italy (2019).

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Concepción Chile (2018).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Sapporo Japan (2016).

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Sydney Australia (rededicated 24 November 1991).

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Nuku'alofa Tonga (rededicated 2007).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose youth joined West Africa's 2010 celebrations of the Book of Mormon's 180th anniversary
prompts.text_original: A country whose youth joined the August 2010 West Africa celebrations of the 180th anniversary of the coming forth of the Book of Mormon
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Liberia (Aug 2010), Benin (dated Aug 2011)
prompts.note: Liberia's chronology dates it August 2010; Benin's says August 2011. 1830 plus 180 is 2010.
prompts.summary: The Book of Mormon was first published in 1830. To mark 180 years, more than 11,000 young people in seven West African countries held celebrations: Liberia, Nigeria, Benin, Togo, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire and Sierra Leone.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Nigeria is named among the seven countries in the celebrations.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Ghana is named among the seven countries in the celebrations.

answers.name: Cote d'Ivoire
answers.fact: Cote d'Ivoire is named among the seven countries.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: Liberia's chronology records the celebrations in August 2010.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: Sierra Leone is named among the seven countries.

answers.name: Benin
answers.fact: Benin's chronology lists its youth among the more than 11,000 taking part.

answers.name: Togo
answers.fact: Togo is named among the seven countries.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a nation made to drink the wine cup of fury in Jeremiah 25 (leave out the Arabian peninsula)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a nation or city made to drink the wine cup of the Lord's fury in Jeremiah 25:17-26 (Jerusalem and Judah, Egypt, the Philistine cities, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, Zidon, Elam, the Medes, and Sheshach); Dedan, Tema, Buz and Arabia are left out because their extent is unclear
prompts.note: Gaza (Azzah) is in Palestine; Ashkelon, Ekron and Ashdod are in Israel. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: Jeremiah is told to take the wine cup of the Lord's fury and make every nation drink it, starting with Jerusalem and ending with Babylon under the cipher Sheshach. Between them come Egypt, the Philistine cities, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Zidon, the kings of Arabia, and Elam and the Medes (Jer 25:15-26).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his princes and all his people drink the cup (Jer 25:19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The cup begins with Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, and includes Ashkelon, Ekron and Ashdod (Jer 25:18, 20).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and the children of Ammon drink it (Jer 25:21).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The king of Sheshach, a coded name for Babylon, drinks after them all (Jer 25:26; compare Jer 51:41).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: All the kings of Tyrus and Zidon drink it (Jer 25:22).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: All the kings of Elam and of the Medes drink it (Jer 25:25).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Azzah, which is Gaza, is among the Philistine cities named (Jer 25:20).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the Americas where a current Presiding Bishopric or Church-wide auxiliary leader served or led a mission.
prompts.text_original: Several general officers serving as of October 2026 (the Presiding Bishopric and the general presidencies of the Relief Society, Young Women, Primary, Young Men and Sunday School) served as missionaries or mission leaders. Pin a country outside the Americas where one of them served, as named in their official biographies.
prompts.summary: General officers often bring mission experience. As of October 2026, Bishop Waddell had served twice in Spain, Bishop Budge twice in Japan, and Brother Wunderli presided over the Cape Verde Praia Mission. Sister Runia and Brother Reid both served as leaders in Sydney, Australia.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Bishop L. Todd Budge: missionary in the Japan Fukuoka Mission, later president of the Japan Tokyo Mission.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Australia Sydney Mission leaders: Sister Tamara W. Runia (2018 to 2021) and Brother Gabriel W. Reid.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Bishop W. Christopher Waddell: missionary in Spain, later president of the Spain Barcelona Mission.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: Brother Paul V. Johnson: missionary in the Norway Oslo Mission.

answers.name: Cape Verde
answers.fact: Brother David J. Wunderli: president of the Cape Verde Praia Mission, 2020 to 2023.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where Latter-day Saint converts were baptized before 1955.
prompts.text_original: Before 1955, Latter-day Saint converts had been baptized in only a few African countries, mostly through the South African Mission. Pin a country where, according to the Church Global Histories, converts were baptized before 1955.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (South Africa, Mauritius, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Zambia)
prompts.note: Nigeria is not scored: a request for missionaries was sent in 1946, but no baptisms are recorded before 1955.
prompts.summary: Missionaries reached Cape Town in 1853 and organized the first branch in Africa at Mowbray. A convert from South Africa baptized six people in Mauritius in 1856. In the 1900s the South African Mission reached members in South West Africa and the Rhodesias, today Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Joseph Patterson and John Dodel, the first converts in South Africa, were baptized at Mowbray, Cape Town, May 26, 1853.

answers.name: Zambia
answers.fact: Johanna and William A. Jubber Jr. were baptized at Ndola in 1947.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: In 1928 near Shangani, Southern Rhodesia, the Jubber family invited mission leaders to baptize their sons.

answers.name: Mauritius
answers.fact: George F. W. Kershaw baptized six converts during a 1856 mission.

answers.name: Namibia
answers.fact: Lawrence C. Ratcliff baptized Johannes and Martha Cloete at Karibib in 1928.
